summary: The Jade Agent Stack is a set of small repositories that share one look and one set of pins.
Vault runs the agent loop and talks to the person; Agent Base keeps identity, data, models and billing; the Kit and UI put an agent on any page.

glossary.def: The part that decides what happens next: the agent loop, schedules and approvals. In Jade this is Vault.
The part that holds what agents use: identity, the database, the model gateway and the audit log. In Jade this is Agent Base.
An exact version (a tag or a commit) that a page or a tool loads, so nothing changes under it.

keyPoints: Every part has one job and one interface.
STACK.md lists the pins; the jade CLI refuses a part with the wrong major version.

items: The **UI/UX** tokens (`--jade-accent`, `--jade-cut`, ...) style every front-end, so a course, a game and a chat look like one product.

chapters.title: Pages from a CDN

maps.title: Lazy loading
links: labs.js | fetches on first run | MicroPython

summary: A stack module is an ES module that finds its own files with `import.meta.url`, so the same code runs from a folder, a webxdc and a CDN.
Big pieces load the first time they are needed: the player, the labs, the teacher, Python and math typesetting.
keyPoints: Load one small entry file; everything else is `import()`-ed on demand.
A CDN URL names a repository, a pin and a path.

items: The load cost grows roughly as $T \approx t_0 + \sum_i s_i / b$ where only the pieces $i$ you use are counted.

quiz.q: How does a module find its own assets on a CDN?
quiz.explain: `new URL('./x', import.meta.url)` resolves next to the module, wherever it was loaded from.

glossary.MicroPython: A small Python 3 for microcontrollers that also compiles to WebAssembly.
